text:
Ava: thinking aloud — proposal: run a lightweight local-catalog-proxy on airgapped clusters that holds staged manifests and lets operators approve component groups before activation.
Sam: interesting. is this different from the existing seed cache + operator gating?
Ava: yes — seed cache is pull-only. proxy would accept signed uploads (from a signed bundle USB/mirror) and expose a small HTTP API for the operator console to review sets. avoids shelling into nodes.
Priya: UX Q: how would approval work for multi-node components (model shards + runtime)? do we gate by component or bundle id?
Ava: gate by activation-group id: a bundle lists groups, each group is a versioned set of artifacts. operator can approve group 1, start canary activation, approve rest.
Marta: what about verifier work? we still need a chain of custody + ephemeral attestation for the node sidecar before activation.
Ava: yep. plan is: proxy verifies bundle signature using escrowed signing keys (KMS/HSM optional), then publishes per-artifact content-addressed metadata. nodes run verifier that does local attest -> operator approves -> proxy marks group as "approved" -> nodes reconcile and activate.
Sam: failure modes? if proxy goes down mid-rollout, do nodes block?
Ava: fallback: nodes can be configured to allow cached-approval-mode if the group was approved earlier or came from a quorum of local caches. default is block to be safe.
Priya: how does this interact with airgap delivery cadence? we often get a mirror disk that contains multiple bundles. operator should be able to stage many bundles offline.
Ava: proxy supports an "import dir" API: place tarballs into /var/lib/local-catalog/import, proxy scans, validates signatures, and creates draft groups for operator review.
Marta: can we get a simple config snippet for operator controls?
Ava: sure:
```yaml
local_catalog:
  import_path: /var/lib/local-catalog/import
  approval_policy: manual # auto|manual|quorum-cache
  quorum_cache_ttl: 72h
  signer_keys: ["/etc/local-catalog/keys/root.pub"]
  allow_cached_activations: false
```
Sam: audit trail? need per-approval signing so we can prove operator X approved group Y at time T.
Ava: proxy will record approvals in an append-only log and sign approval records with a local key; we can optionally mirror logs to a central s3-like store for long-term retention when connectivity exists.
Priya: size/retention: catalogs could hold many model shards — do we GC artifacts?
Ava: propose LRU retention with policy tagging per bundle. operator can pin bundles. GC only removes unpinned artifacts not referenced by an approved group.
Marta: performance: verifier on node side mustn't redownload large blobs during approval. we should rely on local disk dedupe and a content-addressed index.
Ava: exactly — proxy exposes artifact URLs that resolve to local files, nodes use range requests and have a streaming verifier to avoid full copy.
Sam: security: if proxy accepts uploads, how do we prevent an attacker with physical access to USB? escrow of signing keys + signed manifests help but still risky.
Ava: we recommend an HSM for signing in HIGH security installs and enforce operator 2-person approval for critical groups.
ops-bot: reminder — runbook snippet: if proxy process crashes, systemd will restart it; to recover partial imports move /var/lib/local-catalog/import -> import-err and restart import scan.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for test-cluster-3 for group b3a2f1 (50% nodes) :rocket:
Priya: wrap-up questions: who owns shipping the operator UI for approvals? product or eng-platform?
Marta: eng-platform builds minimal API + CLI, product owns console integration. we'll iterate.
Ava: next steps i propose: write short RFC with sequence diagram (import -> verify -> approve -> sign-approval -> node reconcile) and a small PoC that exposes the import dir and approval API. volunteers?
Sam: I'll pair with Ava on the PoC this week.
Priya: i'll sketch the operator flow and acceptance criteria.
Marta: i'll add threat-model notes and approval audit requirements.
Ava: thanks — i'll start the RFC draft, aim for RFC in 3 business days.
